plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks which transcription factors drive the response of the aldosterone-treated kidney samples relative to vehicle controls. The inputs are a single gene-level count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 13 columns — one gene identifier column plus 12 samples) and a sample table (metadata.csv, 12 rows x 2 columns) giving condition for 6 aldosterone-treated and 6 vehicle-control human kidney samples, unpaired, single batch. The length-correction state of the Salmon output is not recorded in the profile, so the plan treats the matrix as a gene-level count table, rounds to integers only where a count model requires it, and records the ambiguity rather than assuming lengthScaledTPM import.

The question is a regulator-activity question, not a differential-expression question, so the walk holds no DE test: activity is inferred per sample on a log matrix and the treatment effect is then tested on the activity scores. T1S1 establishes sample structure first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) — with 6 vs 6 and no batch factor, the only structural risks are an outlier sample or a group split that does not follow condition, and both must be seen before any inference. T1S2 filters low-count genes and produces the log2-CPM matrix that the activity step consumes; the filter matters because a regulon score is a weighted mean over targets and unexpressed targets inject noise. T2S3 runs decoupleR's univariate linear model on the CollecTRI human regulons (present in the reference store at 2.0), keeping the signed mode of regulation so repressor targets lower the score, requiring at least 5 measured targets per regulator, then tests aldosterone vs vehicle on the score matrix with limma and adjusts across regulators with Benjamini-Hochberg. Because CollecTRI is signed and curated it is the first-choice prior; DoRothEA A-C (also present) is run as a sensitivity check so the report can state the overlap and disagreement of the top regulators across two priors. A network cannot be inferred from the expression matrix itself here — 12 samples is far below what mutual-information network inference needs — so a prior-knowledge network is the only sound source of regulons, and the report must say so. T2S4 adds the PROGENy pathway footprint (mlm, top 500 responsive genes) as upstream context, since the mineralocorticoid response is a signalling perturbation and a footprint helps distinguish a direct NR3C2/NR3C1 signal from a generic stress or inflammatory response; it is context, not the answer. T1S5 assembles the report with the reproducibility record and the fields required of an activity inference, stating plainly that an activity score is an inference from a prior network rather than a measurement, and that with n=6 per group a top regulator is a hypothesis for follow-up.

steps.question: Which transcription factors are the defensible candidates for driving the aldosterone response in these 6 vs 6 human kidney samples, and with what stated uncertainty?
steps.description: Assemble a report that answers the research question directly: the ranked transcription factors whose inferred activity differs between the 6 aldosterone-treated and 6 vehicle-control kidney samples, with direction, effect size, BH-adjusted p, and number of measured targets, from both the CollecTRI and the DoRothEA A-C priors, alongside the PROGENy footprint context. Include the QC findings from T1S1 (sample structure, any flagged sample), the gene retention from T1S2, and the required activity-report fields: the network name and version, the input statistic (per-sample log2-CPM), the contrast (aldosterone vs vehicle), the estimator (ulm), the minimum regulon size (5), the number of regulators tested, and the inference caution. Include a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seed, package versions, the regulon collection version, and the annotation release. State plainly what the analysis does not establish.
steps.context: The audience wants a TF shortlist. The honest framing is that these are inferences from a literature-curated prior network on 12 samples, ranked, with the direction of shift — not demonstrated drivers. Where the two priors disagree on a top regulator, say so rather than reporting only the more convenient one.
acceptance_criteria: The report names the ranked candidate transcription factors with direction, effect size, BH-adjusted p, and target count, for both priors
Network name and version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, minimum regulon size, and number of regulators tested are all stated
The report states that an activity score is an inference from a prior network and not a measurement, and that a top regulator is a hypothesis for follow-up
Overlap and disagreement between the two regulon priors is reported, not hidden
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seed, package versions, regulon collection version, and annotation release is included
The report states that no differential expression test was run and that the Salmon length-correction state of the input counts was unrecorded
constraints: Do not present any regulator as an established driver of the aldosterone response
Do not report only the significant regulators — include the full ranked table as a supplement
State the n (6 aldosterone, 6 vehicle) wherever a claim of significance is made
caveats: With 6 per group, absence of BH-significant regulators is a plausible and reportable outcome; report the ranking and the effect sizes in that case rather than lowering the threshold

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step itself; the reporting content follows the reproducibility record of R-0086@becf and the activity-report fields of R-0119@5f4d

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
edgeR filterByExpr on the 12000-gene count matrix
Transcription factor activity with decoupleR ulm on the CollecTRI regulons

parameters.name: activity_report_fields
parameters.value: network_name, network_version, input_statistic, contrast, estimator, min_regulon_size, n_regulators_tested, inference_caution

violations.message: filterByExpr low count filter (edgeR) is not a permitted method for filter_low_counts in this situation.
permitted: Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
